# Project plan

## Start-up phase
<!--
Covering the planning phase, this section should provide a relatively
detailed plan of how work will start on the project. This section is
important because projects need to get up and running quickly.


 - [ ] Setting up collaboration platform inc. code for contributors etc.
 - [ ] License decisions
 - [ ] Reporting framework
-->
During Month 1, the Project Lead and Co-Lead will confirm responsibilities and user requirements, finalise the statistical and technical specification, agree the minimum viable product and site-results structure, and establish the public repository, open-source licence, issue tracker and automated testing framework.


## Technical delivery
<!--
Covering the actual delivery of the project this section should
provide at least a high-level description of the implementation.

Including target dates is really important as you need to be committed
and the ISC need to have a means of tracking delivery
-->
| Period | Activities and milestones | Lead |
|---|---|---|
| Month 1 | Finalise user requirements, specification, repository, licence and test plan. | Lead & Co-Lead |
| Months 2–3 | Develop mapping, audit and local-validation functions; release alpha version. | Lead & RA |
| Months 4–5 | Develop synthetic multisite datasets and site-results schema; verify statistical methods and implement automated tests. | Project team |
| Month 6 | Develop compatibility checks, central synthesis, heterogeneity assessment and reproducible reporting; release beta version. | Project team |
| Month 7 | Complete an end-to-end demonstration using a public real-world dataset partitioned into simulated sites. | Project team |
| Month 8 | Conduct structured user testing and, subject to approvals, explore testing in Brazilian intensive care settings or within the ISARIC research network. | Co-Lead & Contributor |
| Month 9 | Complete independent statistical verification and code review; resolve critical issues and prepare a release candidate. | Project team & independent reviewer |
| Month 10 | Complete tutorials, contributor documentation and governance guidance; publish and disseminate the reproducible release. | Project team |

Progress will be managed through monthly meetings, repository milestones, issue tracking, code review and continuous integration.

## Other aspects

<!--
How will you ensure that your work is available to the widest number
of people? Please specify the open-source or creative commons license(s)
you will use, how you will host your code so that others can contribute,
and how you will publicize your work. We encourage you to plan content
to be shared quarterly on the R Consortium blog.

 - [ ] Announcement post
 - [ ] Delivery blog post
 - [ ] Social media
 - [ ] UseR!
 - [ ] ISC meetings
-->
Development will occur publicly on GitHub under an appropriate open-source licence, with issue tracking, contribution guidance and automated testing to support community participation. The core package will use synthetic data; any real-data testing will require relevant ethical, institutional and data-access approvals, with patient-level data remaining locally controlled. The team will disseminate major milestones and the final release through relevant R-community channels, including opportunities provided by the R Consortium. The Project Lead and Co-Lead will maintain the package after the grant, supported by automated tests, developer documentation and community contributions.

## Budget & funding plan

<!--
Note that the maximum grant is $10k USD. The proposal should be in USD.

Outline the milestones for development and how much funding will be
required for each stage (as payments will be tied to project milestone
completion). This also helps the ISC in the event of partial funding. 
Each milestone should specify the work to be done and the
expected outcomes, providing enough detail for the ISC to understand
the scope of the project work and assess the likelihood of success.

We expect that most of the budget will be allocated
for labor costs. We do not cover indirect costs. The ISC grants cannot
cover such things as travel, lodging, food, journal publication fees,
or personal hardware. Cloud services may be covered if they are specific
to the project and the project period. The ISC reserves the right to vet
how funds are used for each project separately. If in doubt, please reach
out to us.
-->
The project requests **US$5,500** over 10 months. Most funding supports research-assistant time for software development, synthetic-data preparation, testing, documentation and repository maintenance. Project-specific cloud services will support development and demonstration during the grant period, and user-testing support will enable structured feedback and refinement.

| Budget item | Amount (US$) | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Research Assistant | 4,500 | US$450/month × 10 months for programming, synthetic-data preparation, testing, documentation and demonstration support |
| Project-specific cloud services | 500 | US$50/month × 10 months for development, testing and demonstration |
| User-testing support | 500 | Structured testing, feedback collection and interface/documentation refinement |
| **Total** | **5,500** | |

Funding can be released against agreed milestones, with early payments supporting specification and local-workflow development, intermediate payments supporting synthetic evaluation and central synthesis, and final payments supporting user testing, verification, documentation and public release.
